finding: Batch 2 source discovery selected UK eMC SmPCs on document quality alone, without checking that the strength each SmPC describes is actually dispensed in Kosovo. Only 12 of 25 substances have a Kosovo product at the SmPC's exact strength, so exact product binding cannot be completed for the remaining 13 no matter how good the extraction is.
rule: Never bind a rule derived from one strength to a product of a different strength. dose_products_v3 carries numerator_value/denominator_value and the dose engine calculates from them, so a cross-strength binding produces a wrong dose rather than a missing one.

blocked.detail: Registry keys bisoprololfumarate, which has 6 products at exactly the 10 mg the SmPC describes. But sections 4.1 and 4.2 never name the salt, so whether that 10 mg is fumarate or base is unproven.
Registry keys cetirizinedihydrochloride (7 products at 10 mg). Section 4.2 says only "1 tablet (10 mg) once daily" and never names the salt.

Registry keys diclofenacsodium (55 products), and section 4.2 names the salt itself: "Adults: One 100 mg diclofenac sodium prolonged-release tablet daily". Six registry products match 100 mg prolonged-release exactly.
Registry keys levothyroxinesodium (16 products at 50 micrograms). The archived sections never name the salt, and microgram dosing makes an unproven assumption especially unsafe.
Kosovo stocks 10, 20 and 40 mg film-coated tablets. No 80 mg.
Kosovo stocks 500 mg film-coated tablets plus infusion and drop presentations. No 250 mg tablet.
11 dexamethasone products, none at 2 mg soluble tablet.
9 furosemide products, none matching the 10 mg/mL injection concentration as written.
Kosovo stocks 50 and 100 mg. No 12.5 mg.
3 ondansetron products, none at 4 mg film-coated tablet.
3 tramadol products, none at 50 mg hard capsule.

next: Three fixes, not one. (1) diclofenac is source-proven and needs only a clinical sign-off on the prepared equivalence proposal. (2) bisoprolol, cetirizine and levothyroxine are blocked on archiving SmPC section 2, which requires changing the parser and the section_code constraint together. (3) The nine strength blocks need source discovery rerun against strengths the Kosovo registry actually carries; no equivalence work reaches them. Binding stays empty for all thirteen until their own fix lands.
saltEvidenceFinding: Only one of the four canonical-key blocks can be closed with archived evidence. The salt and strength basis is declared in SmPC section 2, and the pipeline cannot reach it: lib/smpc-parser.js parses 4.1-4.9 only, and dose_source_sections_v3 constrains section_code to ^4\.[1-9]$ so section 2 could not be stored even if parsed. Proposals recorded in data/drx-batch2-salt-equivalence-proposals-v1.json.
routeRule: Never bind a rule derived from an oral SmPC to a product of another route, and never across release profiles. Section 4.2 of an oral label states an oral regimen, so a registry product at the same strength given intravenously is a different medicine for dosing purposes; a prolonged-release regimen is likewise not interchangeable with an immediate-release one. Measured live, 34 exact-strength matches are 32 route-compatible and 2 route-excluded, both pantoprazole 40 mg parenteral forms that strength-only matching would have bound to oral 4.2 dosing.
